summary: Crestline is approaching renewal for their Redwood Dedicated commitment and is evaluating an expansion: extra capacity (2x GPUs), adding east-us region, and a one-year contract extension. Main concerns are predictable latency for low-latency payment flows, data residency/compliance, and cost tradeoffs between hosted bursts vs reserved capacity. SE will run benchmarks and Redwood to send quote + SOC2 docs.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Redwood CSM); Mark Rivers (Crestline Head of Platform), Jenna Lee (SRE Lead), Omar Ruiz (CTO), Nina Patel (Procurement)

Summary: quick check-in ahead of renewal; customer wants capacity and region expansion options + compliance artifacts.

00:00:05 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um, quick roll call, we have Priya and Maya from our side, and, Mark do you want to kick off?
00:00:14 Mark Rivers: Yeah thanks Alex, appreciate it. So the purpose here is, uh, we are coming up on our renewal and we wanted to talk through capacity options and adding east-us as a region for lower latency to our customers on the east coast. Also want to confirm SOC2 stuff for procurement.
00:00:30 Alex Kim: Great, yep. high level, we can do dedicated capacity bump or you can add hosted burst to the existing plan. Priya, can you speak to perf differences?
00:00:40 Priya Desai: Sure, um, so dedicated gives you the most predictable p99 latency and throughput. We've seen, in similar banking workloads, about 20-30% reduction in tail latency compared to multi-tenant hosted plans, especially under sustained QPS. The trade off is cost — reserved capacity is committed but more predictable.
00:00:58 Jenna Lee: Just to interrupt—how large of an increase are we talking about? our current commit is 4 A100-like GPUs. If we double that, what kind of cost delta and are we locked in?
00:01:12 Alex Kim: Good question. For a 2x increase we can model two options: 1) extend the reserved commit for 12 months at a non-linear discounted rate, or 2) keep current commit and add burstable hosted capacity for peak hours. We'll put numbers in the quote.
00:01:28 Nina Patel: Procurement note: we need the contract amendment language, and the SOC2 + ISO docs attached. Also need clarity on data retention and KMS/HSM integration for keys.
00:01:40 Maya Torres: We'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts today, and there are standard KMS integration docs. For HSM-backed key stores, that's part of our private deployment add-on — but we do support customer-managed KMS keys in Dedicated via our KMS integration.
00:01:56 Omar Ruiz: For our latency targets it's mostly p99 under 250ms end-to-end for our payment API calls. Is that achievable with dedicated in east-us?
00:02:06 Priya Desai: Yes, that's what we typically tune for. We'll need realistic traffic profiles — prefix cache hit rates, average token lengths — if you can share those we can configure batching and KV cache to meet the SLO.
00:02:18 Mark Rivers: We can provide traffic snapshots. We expect 150 QPS sustained with spikes up to 600 during batch windows.
00:02:27 Priya Desai: Good, that's helpful. We'll run a benchmark with that profile on a dedicated pool in east-us. Expect to test generation latency and throughput, and then we'll share detailed numbers.
00:02:36 Alex Kim: Sounds good. On the timeline: renewal is end of May, is that right Mark?
00:02:42 Mark Rivers: Correct; we'd like to finalize by May 20 if possible.
00:02:46 Alex Kim: Ok, that gives us a few weeks. We'll aim to get the quote and perf data before then.
00:02:51 Jenna Lee: A couple of security questions — audit logs retention, SSO/SAML details, and do you provide per-token audit trails?
00:02:59 Maya Torres: We capture request/response metadata and can configure retention windows. We also offer event-level audit logs for Dedicated/Private customers and we can expose them into your SIEM. SSO/SAML and SCIM are supported for RBAC.
00:03:11 Nina Patel: Great, send all that in writing please.
00:03:14 Alex Kim: Will do. Any concerns about multiregion routing? If we add east-us, we typically route traffic by region with a failover policy back to primary. There are options for sticky routing or session-level affinity if needed.
00:03:27 Omar Ruiz: Sticky routing would help for stateful sessions, especially around KV cache. Also, how does cache warm-up work across regions?
00:03:33 Priya Desai: KV cache is per-region; we can seed caches using warm-up jobs but cross-region cache replication isn't automatic. For low-latency you want local cache hits — which is why routing and seeding matter.
00:03:45 Mark Rivers: Cost question again — if we seed caches and have duplicates across regions does that multiply memory costs?
00:03:51 Priya Desai: Yes some memory duplication is expected; we'll show that in the cost model, and there are quantization and model shard options that reduce memory footprint.
00:04:00 Alex Kim: One point on procurement — we can do an amendment for a 12-month extension on top of your existing term to cover the reserved bump, or a separate SOW for a pilot. Which would you prefer?
00:04:11 Nina Patel: Amendment is better; it keeps one contract. But we need clear exit and rollback terms in case perf doesn't meet SLO.
00:04:19 Maya Torres: We can include a pilot clause: if benchmarks don't meet the agreed SLOs, we can adjust pricing or provide credits. We'll put suggested language in the amendment.
00:04:28 Mark Rivers: That addresses my worry.
00:04:30 Jenna Lee: For the benchmark — can we request both p50/p95/p99 and tail percentiles for different payload sizes? small prompts vs long completions?
00:04:39 Priya Desai: Yep, absolutely. We'll run a small prompt set and a long prompt set, and include token-level breakdown. Also we'll include cost per 1k tokens estimates under different batching configs.
00:04:51 Mark Rivers: Anything about compliance we need to know for east-us region? data residency rules?
00:04:55 Maya Torres: East-us region will host customer data within that region. If you have specific residency controls we'll note them in the contract. For stronger regulatory controls we can discuss Private deployment options, but that adds complexity.
00:05:07 Omar Ruiz: We're not at Private yet, but we might consider it long-term. For now dedicated + region expansion is fine.
00:05:13 Alex Kim: Good. Next steps recap — Alex to send quote and amendment draft; Priya to run benchmark in east-us; Maya to share SOC2/ISO and KMS docs. Customer will share traffic profiles and confirm final QPS targets.
00:05:26 Mark Rivers: Sounds good. Anything else?
00:05:29 Nina Patel: Just timelines — we need docs by end of week to review with legal.
00:05:33 Alex Kim: We'll prioritize. Thanks all.
00:05:36 (meeting ends)
notes: Redwood to offer 12-month amendment with pilot clause
SE to benchmark dedicated pool in east-us with 150 QPS baseline and spikes to 600 QPS
SOC2/ISO artifacts to be shared immediately
